metadata.title: PCR-1000: Addgene Standard PCR Protocol (Detailed)
metadata.purpose: Amplify a defined DNA region in vitro by Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) using a heat-resistant DNA polymerase originally isolated from Thermus aquaticus (Taq). The reaction exploits repeated cycles of heating and cooling: denaturation separates the double-stranded template, annealing allows two synthetic oligonucleotide primers to hybridize upstream (5') and downstream (3') of the target, and extension lets the polymerase synthesize new complementary strands from free deoxyribonucleotides (dNTPs provided in equal molar ratio). Each cycle approximately doubles the target, yielding thousands of copies from a single starting molecule. This protocol describes a standard 50 uL Taq-style endpoint PCR reaction based on the Addgene PCR protocol.
metadata.scope: Standard endpoint PCR using Taq polymerase. Not validated for qPCR quantitation, RT-PCR, or high-fidelity cloning workflows. For related procedures see Addgene protocols on primer design, plasmid cloning by PCR, gel electrophoresis, restriction digest of plasmid DNA, and DNA ligation.
beforeYouBegin: Keep all reagents on ice during setup to maintain enzyme activity.
Use thin-walled PCR tubes for optimal heat transfer in the thermal cycler.

Design primers using tools such as Primer3. Ensure primers are 18-24 nt, 40-60% GC content, with Tm within 5 degrees C of each other. Each primer must hybridize to a complementary sequence at the 3' end of the target region and serve as the starting point for DNA elongation.
For multiple reactions, prepare a master mix containing all shared components (except primers and template) with 10% extra volume to account for pipetting loss.
Use a clean workspace with dedicated pre-PCR pipettes and aerosol-resistant tips.
Taq polymerase synthesizes DNA at approximately 1-2 kilobases per minute — use this rate to set extension times based on expected amplicon size.

materials.name: Template DNA
materials.specification: 10-500 ng total; plasmid DNA, genomic DNA, cDNA, or purified amplicon. Contains the DNA region to be amplified; must have sequences complementary to both primers flanking the target segment.

materials.name: 10X Taq buffer with MgCl2
materials.specification: Provides the optimal chemical environment for the polymerase. Contains divalent cations (Mg2+) that stabilize primer-template interactions and are essential cofactors for polymerase activity. Note: higher MgCl2 concentrations can increase polymerase error rate — do not add excess MgCl2 unless troubleshooting requires it.
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: dNTP mix (10 mM each nucleotide)
materials.specification: Equal molar ratio of dATP, dTTP, dGTP, dCTP; final 200 uM each in reaction. These are the building blocks of the new DNA strand — the polymerase adds them individually to the growing chain in an order complementary to the template.
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; avoid repeated freeze-thaw

materials.name: Forward primer
materials.specification: Final 0.5 uM in reaction. A short single-stranded DNA oligonucleotide (typically 18-24 nt) that hybridizes to a complementary sequence at the 3' end of the target region on one strand. Serves as the starting point for DNA elongation by the polymerase.
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: Reverse primer
materials.specification: Final 0.5 uM in reaction. A short single-stranded DNA oligonucleotide (typically 18-24 nt) that hybridizes to a complementary sequence at the 3' end of the target region on the opposite strand. Together with the forward primer, defines the boundaries of the amplified product.
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice during use

materials.name: Taq DNA polymerase
materials.specification: Heat-resistant DNA polymerase originally isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus. Withstands repeated denaturation at 94 degrees C without losing activity. Optimal polymerization activity at approximately 70-72 degrees C. Synthesizes new DNA at approximately 1-2 kilobases per minute. 1 U per 50 uL reaction.
materials.storage: Store at -20 degrees C; keep on ice; do NOT vortex

materials.name: Sterile dH2O
materials.specification: Molecular biology grade; nuclease-free. Fills the remaining reaction volume to 50 uL; provides the aqueous solvent and contributes to buffer capacity.

materials.name: 25 mM MgCl2 (optional)
materials.specification: For optimization if PCR fails; add to increase Mg2+ concentration. Caution: excess MgCl2 can increase polymerase error rate and promote non-specific amplification.

materials.name: DMSO (optional)
materials.specification: For GC-rich templates; aids denaturation of secondary structures that resist melting at standard denaturation temperatures.

equipment.name: Thin-walled PCR tubes
equipment.settings: 0.2 mL thin-walled tubes for optimal heat transfer

tables.title: 50 uL Reaction Setup
rows: Contains the target DNA region to be amplified; must be complementary to primers
Provides optimal chemical environment; Mg2+ stabilizes primer-template duplex and is a polymerase cofactor
Building blocks (dATP, dTTP, dGTP, dCTP) added individually to new strand by polymerase
Hybridizes to template 3' of target on one strand; starting point for elongation
Hybridizes to template 3' of target on opposite strand; defines amplicon boundary
Heat-resistant enzyme (from T. aquaticus) that drives DNA synthesis at ~70 degrees C
Fills remaining volume; provides aqueous solvent and buffer capacity
tables.note: Volumes are for a single 50 uL reaction. For master mix preparation, multiply each volume by (N + 10%) where N is the number of reactions.

tables.title: Cycling Program
rows: Heat breaks hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs, fully denaturing the double-stranded template into single strands
Re-denatures all double-stranded DNA (template and newly synthesized products) each cycle
Forward and reverse primers hybridize to their complementary single-stranded template sequences; DNA polymerase binds to the primer-template duplex
Taq polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands by adding dNTPs complementary to the template, extending from the 3' end of each annealed primer at ~1-2 kb/min
Ensures all partially extended products are completed to full length
Short-term hold; prevents enzyme activity and sample degradation
tables.note: Annealing temperature should be set approximately 5 degrees C below the primer melting temperature (Tm). Extension time depends on amplicon size: Taq polymerase synthesizes DNA at approximately 1-2 kilobases per minute.

tables.title: Master Mix Calculation Example (7 reactions)
tables.note: Multiply reagent volumes by (number of reactions + 10% overage). Primers are added individually to each tube and are NOT included in the master mix.

tables.title: Primer Dilution Guide
rows: Add dH2O in uL equal to (nanomoles x 10) to the lyophilized primer pellet
Dilute 1:10 from 100 uM stock (100 uL stock + 900 uL dH2O)

tables.title: Primer Design Checklist
rows: Longer primers may be required for cloning tails; calculate Tm from the annealing region only
Avoid very low GC, long single-base runs (e.g. AAAA), and strong hairpin structures
Use one consistent Tm calculator for both primers to ensure comparable annealing
Avoid 3' complementarity between forward and reverse primers to prevent primer dimer; a weak GC clamp (1-2 G/C at 3' end) can improve binding
Routine endpoint PCR: 100 bp to several kb; longer products need enzyme-specific extension time optimization

steps.action: Design primers using a tool such as Primer3. Each primer must hybridize to a complementary sequence at the 3' end of the target region and serve as the starting point for DNA elongation by the polymerase. Two unique single-stranded oligonucleotide primers are required: one annealing upstream (5') and one downstream (3') of the DNA segment to be amplified.
steps.expectedResult: Primers designed and diluted to 10 uM working stock.

steps.action: Prepare primer stocks: reconstitute lyophilized primers to 100 uM by adding dH2O (in uL) equal to nanomoles x 10. Then prepare 10 uM working stocks by 1:10 dilution (100 uL of 100 uM stock + 900 uL dH2O).
steps.expectedResult: Forward and reverse primers at 10 uM working concentration.

steps.action: Place thin-walled PCR tubes on ice. Label tubes for each sample, including a no-template control (NTC) and a positive control.
steps.expectedResult: Labeled PCR tubes on ice ready for reagent addition.

steps.action: For multiple reactions, prepare a master mix: multiply each reagent volume by the number of reactions plus 10% extra to account for pipetting error. Combine sterile dH2O, 10X Taq buffer with MgCl2, dNTP mix, and Taq DNA polymerase in a single tube. Mix gently by pipetting up and down. Do NOT include primers or template DNA in the master mix — primers are added to individual tubes because different reactions may use different primer pairs.
steps.criticalNotes: Add polymerase last. Do NOT vortex — mix by gentle pipetting only. Keep on ice at all times.
steps.expectedResult: Homogeneous master mix on ice, ready for aliquoting.

steps.action: Add forward primer (2.5 uL of 10 uM stock) and reverse primer (2.5 uL of 10 uM stock) to each PCR tube individually. Primers are not included in the master mix so that different primer pairs can be used in parallel reactions from the same mix.

parameters.rawText: 2.5 uL each primer (10 uM stock); final 0.5 uM in reaction

steps.expectedResult: Primers dispensed into individual reaction tubes.

steps.action: Add 45 uL of master mix to each tube (50 uL total minus 2.5 uL forward primer minus 2.5 uL reverse primer). Then add template DNA (2 uL, 10-500 ng) last. For the NTC, add sterile dH2O instead of template DNA. The template contains the DNA region to be amplified and must have sequences complementary to both primers.
steps.criticalNotes: Add template last to minimize contamination risk. Load NTC last.
steps.expectedResult: All 50 uL reactions assembled with template added last.

steps.action: Secure tube caps. Gently tap tubes to mix contents and briefly centrifuge to collect liquid at the bottom and remove air bubbles.
steps.expectedResult: Liquid collected at tube bottom, no air bubbles.

steps.action: Place tubes in the PCR machine. Set the annealing temperature to approximately 5 degrees C below the primer melting temperature (Tm). Set extension time to 1-2 minutes per kilobase of expected amplicon length — Taq polymerase synthesizes DNA at approximately 1-2 kilobases per minute. During denaturation (94 degrees C), heat breaks hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs, separating double-stranded DNA into single strands. During annealing (~55 degrees C), the primers hybridize to their complementary sequences and DNA polymerase binds to the primer-template duplex. During extension (72 degrees C), Taq polymerase adds dNTPs to the 3' end of each primer, synthesizing new strands complementary to the template.

parameters.rawText: Initial denaturation: 94 degrees C for 2 min — denatures template, breaks hydrogen bonds
Annealing: ~55 degrees C (Tm - 5 degrees C) for 30 sec — primers bind template, polymerase binds duplex
Extension: 72 degrees C for 1 min/kb — polymerase synthesizes new strand at ~1-2 kb/min

steps.action: Run the cycling program: initial denaturation at 94 degrees C for 2 min (fully denatures template), then 25-30 cycles of denaturation (94 degrees C, 30 sec), annealing (55 degrees C, 30 sec — primers hybridize to single-stranded template and polymerase binds), and extension (72 degrees C, 1 min/kb — Taq synthesizes new complementary strands from dNTPs), followed by a final extension at 72 degrees C for 5 min to ensure all partially extended products are completed to full length.

repeat.notes: 25-30 cycles; adjust based on template abundance and amplicon size

steps.expectedResult: Cycling complete; target DNA amplified exponentially — each cycle approximately doubles the amount of target sequence.

steps.action: Run 2 uL of PCR product on an agarose gel with an appropriate DNA size ladder to verify band size and concentration. A single discrete band at the expected amplicon size indicates successful amplification. The NTC lane should be clean (no target-size band), confirming no contamination. The positive control should show the expected band, confirming that the master mix, cycling program, and detection method are all working.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Single band at expected amplicon size
No target-size band in no-template control — confirms no contamination
Expected band present — confirms master mix, cycling, and detection are functional

steps.expectedResult: Single band at expected size in sample lanes; clean NTC; positive control confirmed.

controls.name: No-template control (NTC)
controls.description: Replace template DNA with sterile dH2O to detect reagent, water, primer, or setup contamination. No target-size band expected.

controls.name: Positive control
controls.description: Use a known template that reliably amplifies to verify that the assay, master mix, template handling, cycling program, and detection method are all working correctly. Expected band should appear.

expectedOutputs: Single band at the expected amplicon size on agarose gel.
Positive control band at expected size.
Complete run record with sample map, reagent lots, cycling program, and gel image.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong annealing temperature, missing component, degraded template, inhibitors in template preparation, insufficient extension time for long amplicons
troubleshooting.solution: Verify setup against the reaction table; lower annealing temperature step-wise or run a gradient; add 1 uL 25 mM MgCl2 and/or 1 uL DMSO per reaction; use fresh enzyme; dilute template to reduce inhibitors; increase extension time for products > 1 kb

troubleshooting.cause: Annealing temperature too low, excess template or primer concentration, nonspecific primer binding to off-target sequences
troubleshooting.solution: Increase annealing temperature step-wise by 1-2 degrees C; reduce template or primer concentration; consider hot-start polymerase; redesign primers with stricter specificity criteria

troubleshooting.cause: Overcycling, degraded template DNA, nonspecific amplification, overloaded gel lane
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce cycle number (try 25 instead of 30); improve template quality (repurify or use fresh prep); optimize annealing temperature; load less product on gel

troubleshooting.cause: 3' complementarity between primers, excess primer concentration relative to template
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce primer concentration to 0.2-0.3 uM; redesign primers to minimize 3' complementarity between forward and reverse primers

troubleshooting.cause: Strong secondary structures in GC-rich regions resist denaturation at standard temperatures
troubleshooting.solution: Increase denaturation time; add 1 uL DMSO per reaction to aid melting of secondary structures; consider specialized GC-rich PCR kits or higher denaturation temperature (98 degrees C with appropriate polymerase)

safety: Ethidium bromide or alternative DNA stains may be mutagenic — wear gloves when handling gels and follow institutional disposal rules.
UV transilluminators emit UV radiation — use eye and skin protection.
